The slow tier matters because of mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, which route each token to only some experts rather than applying the full weights to every token. Input distribution can therefore change what work is done. The authors observed that randomly initialized data activated 13–38% more experts than real data, and that this caused a 1.3× end-to-end slowdown in the engine. This is the paper's motivation for not trusting isolated, random-input kernel measurements. Systems such as GEAK [...] and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). On the other hand, systems use agents to directly optimize end-to-end engines but suffer from slow engine launch times. To address these challenges, we build Together Compiler (TKCC), the first truly continual agent loop designed for AI inference optimization. To [...] ## Audio

## 1. Scale AI

Scale AI is one of the best-known names in AI data services. It does data annotation, data curation, model evaluation, and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), and its work feeds into large language models (LLMs), computer vision, robotics, and defense projects. In May 2026, its US Department of War agreement grew from USD 100 Million to a potential USD 500 Million, which puts it in a strong spot for government and defense AI work.

## 2. Surge AI [...] ## 2. Surge AI

Surge AI’s specialty is human feedback and high-quality data for advanced models. It offers RLHF, expert annotation, preference data, and model evaluation across text, images, audio, and video. Developers who need real human judgment to make their models better tend to rely on it. Surge AI reported USD 1.2 Billion in revenue for FY2024, but keep in mind that this isn’t verified 2026 revenue.

## 3. Mercor [...] 2. Which are the top AI training data providers in 2026?

The top 10 include Scale AI, Surge AI, Mercor, Innodata, Appen, TELUS Digital, iMerit, Turing, micro1, and Prolific.

3. What services do AI training data companies offer?

These companies offer data annotation, RLHF, expert feedback, multilingual datasets, model evaluation, and specialist data preparation.

4. Why do AI companies need human feedback?
